Both the object and the trailing "up" are optional, so "I can't wake him" matches too. . This is the turn that now escalates the incident, on the FIRST thing the caller says, rather than turn 3. triage.note: The responder asserts breathing. phrases.py must fire inadequate_breathing on "gasping" REGARDLESS, because agonal respiration is an arrest presentation. This assertion is the entire reason the marker exists.

t03.script: He's not — no, he's not responding, I'm shaking him and shouting at him and there's nothing.

triage.note:
F-001 FIXED. "He's not — no, he's not responding" now fires `unresponsive`. . The self-repair "no," used to land inside a flat 3-word lookback and was read as a logical negation of the finding after it. It is not: it is a discourse marker meaning "no, in answer to your question". The lookback is now clause-scoped — it stops at punctuation and at coordinating conjunctions — and within the clause a negator only governs the finding if it reaches it across nothing but function words. Here the "no" has to cross a fresh subject and verb ("he's"), so it does not suppress. Verified:
    "he's not responding"                -> unresponsive
    "he's not - no, he's not responding" -> unresponsive
    "no he's not breathing"              -> not_breathing
    "no, no, he's not breathing"         -> not_breathing
. The adjacent negations this rule must still suppress do:
    "the casualty is not unresponsive"   -> NONE
    "he's never had a cardiac arrest"    -> NONE
. Previously asserted as observed: expect_markers [].

s10_poolside_drowning.title: Child pulled from a swimming pool

t01.script: We've pulled a little boy out of the pool, he's not moving, he's not breathing, oh god, he's four, he's only four —

triage.note:
TWO DEFECTS FIXED ON ONE TURN. All three markers now fire; before, exactly one did. . F-001 (adjacent-clause negation) FIXED: "he's not moving, he's not breathing" now fires BOTH `unresponsive` and `not_breathing`. The negation lookback is clause-scoped, so the "not" belonging to "not moving" no longer reaches across the comma to suppress the later finding. Reporting two life threats in one breath no longer makes the second one vanish. Verified:
    "he's not moving, he's not breathing" -> [not_breathing, unresponsive]
    "no pulse, he's not breathing"        -> [not_breathing, no_pulse]
. F-004 (drowning vocabulary) FIXED: the pattern now matches a named submersion location rather than the literal word "water", and requires the casualty to be the OBJECT of the extraction. Verified:
    "pulled a little boy out of the pool" -> [drowning]
    "we dragged her out of the lake"      -> [drowning]
    "he got out of the pool and sat down" -> NONE
`drowning` firing is what signals the hypoxic-arrest sequence — five rescue breaths BEFORE compressions — which inverts adult BLS and is the whole reason a separate drowning protocol exists. . This turn is why the corpus asserts all three layers: criticality reached 5 via `unresponsive` even while two independent failures sat underneath a correct-looking level. . Previously asserted as observed: expect_markers [unresponsive].

s11_platform_negation.title: Negation — the casualty is NOT unresponsive

t01.script: A bloke's just fainted on the platform. He went down but he's come round now — he's not unresponsive, he's talking to me.

triage.note: "not unresponsive" — the negation window suppresses the match. If unresponsive fires here, a fainting passenger triggers a clinician bridge and the system is crying wolf.

stt.transcript: A bloke just landed on the platform. He went down. He's come around now. He's not unreported. He's talking to me.

t02.script: He wasn't breathing properly for a second there but he is breathing now, he's fine, he's sat up against the wall.

triage.note: F-002 FIXED. "wasn't breathing ... but he is breathing now" is a recovery narrative and is now suppressed, as the module's own docstring always said it should be. . The guard required a bare `was|were|had` token BEFORE the match. Here the past tense is fused into "wasn't", and "wasn't breathing" is itself the matched text, so there was nothing past-tense in front of the match at all. The tense is now read from the start of the match as well as from the word before it, and the contracted auxiliaries are in the same set as the bare ones. . This is the ONE fix in this set that narrows firing, so it is deliberately the tightest: suppression still requires BOTH the past tense AND an explicit later contradiction. "He wasn't breathing, I've started CPR" — past tense, no contradiction — still fires. . Previously asserted as observed: expect_markers [not_breathing] at level 5, which bridged a clinician to a recovered faint.

stt.transcript: Ah, he wasn't breathing properly for a 2nd there, but he is breathing now. He's fine. He's out against the wall

t03.script: No he's never had a cardiac arrest or anything like that, he says he just skipped breakfast.

triage.note: The marker assertion here is the real subject: "never had a cardiac arrest" is negated, so `cardiac_arrest` correctly stays silent. A history question must not escalate a live incident. That suppression survived the F-001 rewrite because the negator reaches the finding across nothing but an auxiliary and a determiner ("never had a"), which is what "the negator governs the finding" means — unlike the discourse "no" of "no, he's not breathing". . Criticality is now 3, which is what this recovered faint clinically warrants. It was 5 as a CONSEQUENCE OF DEFECT F-002 on turn 2 — the contracted-past-tense miss escalated the incident and the ratchet correctly refused to bring it back down. . That is still the clearest illustration of why the ratchet and the marker logic must be tested together: one bad escalation was permanent for the rest of the incident.

stt.transcript: No. He's never had a cardiac arrest or anything like that. He just he gives breakfast.

t04.script: He's a bit pale and clammy still. Should he be sat up or lying down?

triage.note: An ordinary recovering faint, assessed as one. This turn used to sit at 5 with a clinician bridged, pinned there by F-002 on turn 2. The scenario now holds Level 3 throughout, which is the whole point of asserting suppression: a net that escalates every recovered faint gets ignored when a real arrest arrives.
